title: OrbACE: Orbital and Atomic Cluster Expansion
abstract: arXiv:2611.33743v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Accurate electronic-structure reference data are expensive, motivating interatomic potentials that learn effectively from limited training sets. We introduce OrbACE (Orbital and Atomic Cluster Expansion), a framework that supplements an E(3)-equivariant cluster-expansion backbone with inexpensive electronic-structure descriptors. On ANI-1x at the $\omega$B97X/6-31G* level, its atom-centered variant, OrbACE-A, trained on 10,000 configurations and evaluated on 442,000 held-out configurations, achieves energy and force mean absolute errors of 3.16 meV/atom and 76 meV/angstrom in direct learning, compared with 9.61 meV/atom and 146 meV/angstrom for MACE with matched backbone settings. This reduces the energy error by a factor of three and approximately halves the force error. Its energy error is also below that of the best delta-corrected MACE baseline, 5.00 meV/atom, although its force error is slightly higher. Combining OrbACE-A with a H

tldr: OrbACE框架通过在E(3)等变簇展开骨干网络中引入廉价的电子结构描述符，在有限训练数据下将能量误差降低至MACE的三分之一、力误差大约减半，显著提升了机器学习原子间势的精度。
en_tdlr: OrbACE augments an E(3)-equivariant cluster-expansion backbone with inexpensive electronic-structure descriptors, cutting the energy error threefold and roughly halving the force error compared to MACE when learning from limited training data.
